source_review.notes: Checked current or explicitly versioned official Apache Spark RDD, checkpoint, streaming, and configuration documentation; the primary RDD paper; Ray task fault-tolerance documentation; Dask resilience documentation; Apache Flink recovery documentation; Apache Beam execution semantics; Apache Hadoop MapReduce documentation; Google Cloud Dataflow exactly-once guidance; Bazel remote-cache documentation; and the OpenLineage object-model specification. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Runtime-specific recomputation guarantees are attributed.

evidence: Reviewed lineage DAG, exact parent mapping, target/available/root sets, recompute closure, transformation digests/costs, closure/loss costs, recovery amplification, failure probability, and materialization/storage costs.
Checked least-closure, cost-sum, amplification, topological induction, and expected checkpoint-value expressions with explicit scopes.
Checked that logical dataset/partition, physical attempt/location, executed plan, cache, durable materialization, checkpoint, root input, and governance provenance remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The model is partition-granular and treats stable root identity, transformation determinism, and boundary integrity as proof premises.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced target report, recompute set filter/join/parse/report/right, reusable set left/raw, and 105 work units.
Recomputed closure work as parse 20 + filter 15 + right 25 + join 40 + report 5 = 105, excluding materialized left.
Checked checkpoint examples distinguish 100 replayed iterations after epoch 900 from the original 1000-epoch lineage and 990/10 surviving/missing shuffle parents.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No universal lineage depth, checkpoint interval, replication factor, cache policy, recovery-amplification, or RTO threshold is prescribed.

evidence: Verified backward closure includes required unavailable ancestors, deduplicates shared parents, and stops exactly at compatible verified roots/materializations.
Verified replay equivalence by topological induction over exact parent versions and deterministic transformations.
Verified a complete equivalent materialization cuts its upstream subgraph and checkpoint economics must remain subordinate to hard durability/RTO constraints.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Path existence, operator names, or today's optimized plan cannot substitute for exact boundary and executed-dependency evidence.

evidence: Reviewed missing/corrupt/expired roots, cache eviction, partial checkpoints, narrow/wide dependencies, lost map/reducer partitions, shared ancestors, skew splitting, and adaptive-plan mismatch.
Reviewed deep and iterative lineage, local versus durable checkpoints, null/NaN/schema/partitioner/serializer changes, and concurrent cleanup/coordinator recovery.
Reviewed time, randomness, locale, time zone, unordered/floating-point reductions, library/runtime drift, mutable remote lookup, and duplicated external effects.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Broken determinism or missing roots produces explicit unrecoverability or a new computation, never silent substitution of current inputs.

evidence: Traced logical partition and graph/executed-plan identity, exact parents/dependency type, root snapshot/offset, code/config/environment, schema/partitioner/serializer, seed, and output digest.
Checked boundary completeness/checksum/coverage/retention, topological scheduling, wide-shuffle mappings, adaptive epochs, explicit iteration versions, and side-effect winner commit.
Checked coupled retention across lineage, inputs, code, schema, shuffle, checkpoints, consumers, retries, branches, audit, and recovery leases.
invariant_checking.notes: Governance provenance may outlive executable artifacts and is labeled non-executable when exact recovery inputs expire.

evidence: Reviewed closure-minimality, replay-equivalence, materialization-cut, and checkpoint-value arguments with explicit graph, stability, and cost assumptions.

Checked counterexamples for dataset-level lineage, mutable roots, missing semantic digests, incomplete caches, whole-graph expansion, under-expanded shuffle, regenerated adaptive plans, and replayed APIs.

Checked fault injection deletes/corrupts partitions and boundaries, expires roots, changes environment, races cleanup, loses shuffle, replays iterations, and compares outputs/effects with a reference.
proof_review.notes: Minimal closure, output equivalence, recoverability, checkpoint durability, and economic value require separate evidence.

evidence: Audited execution lineage, provenance lineage, logical node, partition, attempt, narrow/wide dependency, materialization, cache, checkpoint, root, truncation, and closure terminology.
Confirmed logical plan, executed adaptive plan, transformation digest, physical block mapping, graph epoch, and iteration/superstep are distinguished.
Confirmed recomputation, task retry, state restore, replication, external-effect deduplication, and compensation are separate mechanisms.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Spark, Ray, Dask, Flink, Beam, Hadoop, Dataflow, Bazel, and OpenLineage concepts are not presented as identical runtime contracts.

evidence: Reviewed graph depth/edges, root/boundary coverage, cached/materialized bytes, closure nodes/partitions/bytes, deduplication, CPU/I/O/shuffle, amplification, equality, recovery time, and checkpoint cost.
Confirmed segmentation by dataset/operator, graph/plan/code version, input cohort, cache/boundary state, failure domain/type, equality relation, and observation horizon.
Confirmed cache hit, small closure count, low storage cost, equal row count, semantic tolerance, and end-to-end recovery latency are separately reported.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: A successful rerun is not mislabeled as minimal, deterministic, bitwise equal, side-effect safe, or economically preferable.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed lineage representation, narrow/wide dependencies, backward closure, root replay, determinism, boundary validation, shuffle/adaptive execution, iteration/state, checkpoint economics, side effects, retention, and verification.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable partition IDs and mappings, canonical digests, closure traversal, boundary manifests, pinned source contracts, deterministic seeds/order, adaptive plan persistence, checkpoint validation, stable effect intents, reachability cleanup, metrics, and fault injection. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from executable lineage and closure through determinism and materialization to economics and retention. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover narrow/wide recovery, shared parents, partial checkpoints, mutable roots, seeds, adaptive layouts, iteration, effects, and evidence.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark/Ray/Dask/Flink/Beam/Hadoop/Dataflow/Bazel/OpenLineage maintainer or RDD-paper author, scheduler/runtime/storage/platform/SRE/security specialist, production workload operator, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
